#151842. From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • In a recent development, the smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

In a recent development, the smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

But disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on latest experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he remarked.

Industry observers note that indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

In a recent development, "We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar remarked.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives indicated stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he said.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar said.

The new study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

Recent findings suggest that inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

According to recent reports, "I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he mentioned, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he noted.

Industry observers note that the research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

Inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he said.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

According to recent reports, "Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

  • Here are the top 10 goalscorers from Europe’s five major leagues (Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Massive names like Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe and Raphinha are leading the scoring charts across Europe so far this season, but there are also some under-the-radar names and even a golden oldie.

Harry Kane was the top scorer in Europe last season with 36 Bundesliga goals, but he surprisingly doesn’t (yet) feature in the top 10 so far this season.

Here are the top 10 goalscorers from Europe’s five major leagues (Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1) this season.

Note: if two players are tied on goals, we’ve ordered them by their minutes-per-goal ratio.

Arguably the most Euro 2020-coded footballer of them all, Schick has retired from international football now but is still banging them in for Bayer Leverkusen.

The 30-year-old Czech striker has scored nine goals in 10 Bundesliga games, including in their 4-0 thrashing of Paderborn last time out.

Nobody expected Paris FC to be sitting second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds of fixtures, but Liam Rosenior is doing a remarkable job in the French capital.

It has been revealed that sinayoko has been central to their unlikely rise. The Mali international scored the winner in their 1-0 win over Auxerre, taking his tally to nine goals in 10 appearances.

Sources indicate that haaland is up to nine goals from his 11 outings of the 2026-27 Premier League campaign. Although he’s drawn blanks in defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

He’s won three Golden Boots in four years since arriving in England and we really can’t see beyond him claiming another this season.

It has been revealed that keep an eye on this lad. Varela is just 21 years old, but he’s already looking like a serious talent at Serie A underdogs Monza, with almost a goal a game in Serie A since his summer move from Benfica.

The Portuguese youngster has been banging in the goals despite his side’s struggles. Surely bigger clubs will be taking notice.

In a recent development, the extraordinary rise continues. Yamal recently declared himself and Mbappe the best two players on the planet, and he might have a point.

Yamal drew a blank in Barca’s first two games of the season, but hit braces in three consecutive games: against Rayo Vallecano, Valencia and Levante.

He’s now reached double figures in La Liga after just 11 appearances, putting him well on course to surpass his previous best goalscoring campaign.

And with nine assists to go alongside those 10 goals, the teenager is doing a pretty good impression of a prime Lionel Messi.

The West Ham striker curse strikes again.

Fullkrug looked a shadow of his former self during his miserable spell in East London, but he’s rediscovered his goalscoring touch back in Germany.

Still technically a West Ham player, the veteran striker has scored 10 goals in 10 Bundesliga appearances since returning to Werder Bremen.

He’s averaging a goal every 83 minutes, a phenomenal return for a player who looked completely finished in the Premier League.

With Harry Kane out until the new year, and Fullkrug already six goals ahead, it’s not unthinkable that the Werder Bremen man beats the Ballon d’Or holder to the Bundesliga Golden Boot. Who saw that coming?

After signing Zabiri in February but seeing him fail to score in his first six games for the club, Rennes sent him on loan to La Liga newcomers Racing Santander for the 2026-27 season.

He’s hit the ground running with nine goals this year, after coming on as a sub in the first two games of the season.

A hat-trick on his first start against Elche justified the decision to include him and he soon added a match-winning brace against Alaves.

Sources indicate that we can safely assume that he won’t be with Racing next season. We wouldn’t be surprised if Rennes cash in, because big-money offers are sure to arrive if he keeps this up.

Malen has been in outstanding form for Roma, scoring 12 goals in just 742 minutes of Serie A football.

The Dutchman is averaging a goal every 61 minutes in the league and also bagged a brace against Real Madrid in the Champions League (albeit in a defeat).

The one-time Aston Villa man is the latest in a long line of strikers to thrive under Gian Piero Gasperini, who has been getting the best out of forwards since Diego Milito at Genoa and later worked wonders with the likes of Duvan Zapata, Luis Muriel and Mateo Retegui at Atalanta.

After finishing runner-up to Harry Kane in the 2026 Ballon d’Or voting, Mbappe is on a mission to make damn sure he gets his hands on the golden ball in 2027.

He has 13 goals from 12 games so far this La Liga season – and he’s only actually needed a handful of those games to get the goals in question.

Mbappe got up and running for the season with a hat-trick against Real Sociedad and has also hit braces against Rayo Vallecano, Sevilla and Barcelona in El Clasico.

Raphinha has been transformed into a striker this season, and it’s working wonders for Barcelona.

The Brazilian has scored an astonishing 15 goals in just 11 La Liga appearances, putting him comfortably clear at the top of Europe’s goalscoring charts.

It has been revealed that he’s averaging a goal every 54 minutes, while his three assists underline that he hasn’t completely abandoned his creative instincts. His momentum was stunted slightly with a knee injury suffered while on international duty, but he’s picked up where he left off with three goals in his last three outings.

Barca could have found themselves with a Lewandowski-shaped void up front this season, but Raphinha is having other ideas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026.

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'.

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr.

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child.

Sources indicate that 'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most key thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

Sources indicate that '(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more notable in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'.

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we’re about a quarter of the way through the 2026-27 Premier League season, but the table is beginning to take shape after nine rounds of fixtures. What do the underlying statistics tell us? Which teams are playing better than their results might suggest, and which teams are overperforming?

Sources indicate that that’s where good old ‘expected goals’, rattler of Proper Football Men across the country, helps us out. We’ve delved into the data to see which teams are doing best and worst in terms of the quality of chances they’ve created and faced.

It has been revealed that brighton & Hove Albion remain among the division’s most prolific attacking sides, but Manchester City surprisingly remain top of the xG charts. Enzo Maresca’s side have created 21.9xG, just ahead of Brighton’s 21.6xG.

The Seagulls are still comfortably outperforming their underlying numbers, having scored 4.4 goals more than their xG suggests they should have.

Creating bagloads of chances and being clinical with them is a pretty deadly combination – although they finally reverted to the mean a bit in their 2-0 smash-and-grab defeat at Hull City, their 2.51xG the highest output of a team who have failed to score this season.

Elsewhere, there’s plenty for new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino to mull over when it comes to their underlying numbers.

The Red Devils are fifth for xG, but their defensive record has deteriorated considerably. They rank second-last for the quality of chances they allow the opposition; them boasting the worst defensive record in Europe’s substantial five leagues is no freak.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool are all unsurprisingly in the top half. Bournemouth are up in third, while Nottingham Forest and Brighton are also among the division’s top six for chances created.

According to recent reports, at the other end, the reigning champions continue to boast comfortably the best defensive numbers in the division. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners have conceded just 9.3xG in 11 matches, 3.2 fewer than second-placed Tottenham.

Arsenal’s ‘expected points’ and xG difference are very healthy as a result, but you’d imagine that Arteta would ideally want them higher than the likes of Manchester United and Nottingham Forest.

Taking a look at the picture as a whole, Carrick’s Manchester United are no longer looking quite so unfortunate. They’ve slipped to 11th for expected goal difference, with a negative xGD of -0.3, and rank 17th for xG against. Their 13 expected points put them 13th in the division.

According to recent reports, the underlying numbers are probably most concerning for Crystal Palace, who sit bottom for xG difference (-8.4) and xG against (23.9). That’s a lot of work for Thomas Frank to rectify. Newcastle United are also struggling, ranking 16th for xG difference, while Hull City have created the fewest expected goals in the division.

Here are all the relevant 2026-27 Premier League tables for xG so far, with the data taken from FotMob.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer remarked he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain noted.

"I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure." Captain Bruno Fernandes gives his immediate reaction to Manchester United's heavy 4-1 defeat to Como 🗣️ 🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/8bzmLGkRAX.

There may be some truth in that, but Carrick’s response felt the most accurate assessment of the lot and will certainly chime with supporters who have long questioned how and why so many United sides, regardless of the manager, reach a point where running, intensity and urgency seem optional. “Whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win,” Carrick remarked.

According to recent reports, carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

United, by contrast, were a sorry collection of strangers. It was impossible to discern a game plan. United were sent out in a strange 4-2-4, with Fernandes and Youri Tielemans operating as almost double false nines. Glenn Hoddle said on TNT Sports that it was like United were “playing in chains”.

Neither looked sure of what they were supposed to be doing. There was just a giant hole where the attack should have been. Everything about them was slow, leaden. The confusion was contagious. Everywhere you looked there were players second-guessing themselves, uncertain of their role and position and habitually a yard or two or three off the pace. But was there any excuse for not running, for so little effort?

The space Paz was afforded to curl in a fine finish less than two minutes in was alarming in the extreme. Carrick brought on Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo for the lamentable Mateus Cunha and Andrey Santos at half-time, but United just got worse.

For Como, who were playing in Italy’s third tier five years ago, this was one of the greatest nights in their history. For United, it was one of the worst. Carrick may pay a heavy price for it, but there are far greater problems than the manager at this football club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After more than a month’s absence, Mile Svilar returned to the pitch, defending Roma’s goal in the match against Parma at the Tardini.

The Giallorossi number 99 then gave an interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio, discussing, among other topics, his relationship with De Rossi and Gasperini.

Industry observers note that the night against Feyenoord in the Europa League in 2024: “That night was the real start of my professional career. From there, everything changed. In those three games—the two against Feyenoord and the one against Frosinone—I started to be a professional. I once told my wife that many goalkeepers start out as second or third-choice, then start playing well due to injuries and start like that. Up until that point, it had happened to me many times in my early years at Benfica, a little less so at Roma, but I never had the feeling inside that it was the right time. “.

“had the feeling that it could never happen to me. But that week, I had it, I felt that my moment had come. A feeling you can’t explain. I felt that something would happen like it does to the others. I knew it was the moment. I never stated it, but I knew it. I had a different adrenaline rush, the feeling of being crucial.”.

“In every job, you need someone who believes in you. And De Rossi was the person who believed in me, who gave me the push. He put me on the field, he had the power to change something, and Daniele changed my life, the life of my family.”.

It has been revealed that “The week before his arrival, I played with AC Milan, but it ended a bit badly. Then we had Verona at home, and during the week I already knew I wouldn’t play. I wasn’t surprised. But he was the first person who called me into his office and mentioned, ‘Look, Mile, I chose not to let you play and let Rui play. But in training, I saw something really interesting, so train because your time will come soon.’ For the first time, someone wanted to explain to me before the match and tell me I wouldn’t play. I immediately felt that he would be different for me.”.

According to recent reports, “De Rossi’s dismissal hurt. I felt bad. He was someone who changed everything for me, in football and therefore in life. I will be grateful to him for the rest of my life.”.

Recent findings suggest that “Last year was spectacular. But there were some low points, and many around us no longer believed in it. But when you keep doing, keep doing, like we’re doing with the coach, it’s something I’ve never seen.”.

“Gasperini’s biggest contribution? The mentality. The physical and tactical work the boys put in because it’s a different way of playing. There’s a winning mentality, which is what we needed because this club truly has everything it takes to do well.”.

“Our objectives? It’s hard to say right now. As everyone can see, we’re doing really well. The tactical and physical work is putting a lot of us ahead. Maybe we were a little behind or something like that before, but now we’re moving up.”.

#151833. Tech Report: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

Tech Report: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1063 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021?
  • What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.
  • Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that remember the NFT boom of 2021? The surge in trading of non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are unique, blockchain-recorded digital assets, was one of the stranger economic offshoots of the COVID-19 pandemic.

What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.

Sources indicate that in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value. The wider cryptocurrency crash was particularly punishing for digital collectibles and largely, they have not recovered.

The sector is worth up to 97% less than it was at its height in January 2022, and sales continue to plummet. So far this year, total global sales of NFTs are less than $2 billion, according to FindWeb3, a cryptocurrency and blockchain jobs platform. That's more than 90% down from the peaks of 2021 and 2022.

In a recent development, does that mean that NFTs will ultimately fade away to nothing, proving right those who dismissed them as a worthless fad? Or is there still some kind of future for them?

Recent findings suggest that "NFTs will still exist, but it will be a niche collectible market," Ben Charoenwong, associate professor of finance at the business school INSEAD, remarked. "This doesn't mean there cannot be booms here and there, but certainly not take off as people had imagined in the past.".

Sources indicate that he thinks whatever future it can have will be "narrow" and says doubt is growing over the value of "non-fungible" as a concept. Non-fungible means an asset is unique and cannot be traded like for like, whereas fungible means it can be traded like for like, for example, with money.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

He notes that the recent trend of financial institutions converting real-world financial assets, such as bonds and stocks, into digital tokens recorded on a blockchain — the so-called tokenization boom — mostly relates to fungible assets.

However, Andrea Barbon, a finance professor at the University of St Gallen in Switzerland, thinks part of NFTs' future lies in this tokenization boom, as there are some examples of people trading unique real-world assets as NFTs.

According to recent reports, "NFT technology is really about ownership," he says. "They describe the ownership of a specific asset that could be a digital asset or real-world asset." He says things like real-estate contracts, expensive watches, artworks or luxury sports cars can now be tokenized, with NFTs created to represent these physical objects.

That immediately begs the question: Why would anyone want to have a digital, NFT version of their watch or sports car?

"Some people want to just speculate on the value of the physical asset and for them, it's great that you don't need to move the physical object around," Barbon said.

"If the object is a nice painting and you buy it from the US, you want to ship it to the UK, that's very costly, it's hassle and it's potentially not safe if the value of this painting is very high," he explained.

He says some companies, such as Courtyard.io, keep physical vaults to hold physical assets which are traded online as NFTs. He says very often, the owner has no interest in having physical possession of the asset.

Another area where he sees some promise for the future of NFTs is connected to artificial intelligence. He claims NFTs could help with AI safety, as they could be used to provide unique, verifiable, non-fungible identities for AI agents.

Ethereum and other blockchain providers are in the process of trying to build NFT systems that would represent and verify AI agents, something Barbon claims could be very successful.

He envisages a scenario where AI agents are recorded on an NFT blockchain and can then be identified and rated for safety and reliability.

"Everybody else can then see that the AI agent is actually doing well, you can trust it, it's safe," he says. "In order to do that, you need something which is uniquely attached to each AI agent and that can be an NFT.".

Another possible use he sees for NFTs in the AI era is that writers and artists could tokenize their work as NFTs so that if an AI agent ends up using it for training, the original work can be more easily identified as unique to the creator.

"Maybe you could then claim that the AI company has to pay you because they have used your content," Barbon states.

While the NFT craze of 2021 can now be seen as a classic bubble, many of those who invested in it have moved on to memecoins and other forms of fungible cryptocurrency, according to Ben Charoenwong.

"Overall, I think the market did not reject blockchains; it rejected non-fungibility," he claims.

At the time of the craze, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said NFT popularity was "100% based on the greater fool theory," the idea being that one can make money through the purchase of overvalued, fundamentally worthless assets as long as there is a"greater fool" willing to pay even more.

In a recent development, one of the most famous NFT collections was the Bored Ape Yacht Club, a series of drawings of apes in various locations in various states of boredom. "Obviously, expensive digital images of monkeys are going to improve the world immensely," Gates joked.

Industry observers note that in many ways, that collection's current status epitomizes NFTs' fall from grace better than anything else. Although it remains one of the biggest NFT marketplaces, its value has plunged.

Recent findings suggest that the singer Justin Bieber bought one image for 500 ETH (Ethereum), or around $1.3 million dollars. The value fell by around 99% to around $14,000. He still owns it.

Yet the fact that these images still command such prices shows they are not entirely worthless. That offers some hope to those who still believe in the technology. Alongside other possible applications linked to AI and tokenization, NFTs may still have a future, albeit a more modest one than when they first came to public attention.

Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (846 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor.
  • Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.
  • According to recent reports, his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

According to recent reports, his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil unveiled on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

But luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Industry observers note that even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

He always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

Janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

Industry observers note that there is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

The "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

Recent findings suggest that his iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Recent findings suggest that guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always remarked that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

From 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

In a recent development, like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

Latest Update: Bradley Barcola should take Thierry Henry’s advice over inability to shoot

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Bradley Barcola was being created at the football factory, shooting was clearly a Friday afternoon job.
  • Recent findings suggest that there is a lot to like about Liverpool’s third most expensive signing of all time.
  • It has been revealed that that kind of pace should make Barcola one of the most feared wingers in the Premier League, the kind of player that full-backs dread playing against.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Bradley Barcola was being created at the football factory, shooting was clearly a Friday afternoon job.

Recent findings suggest that there is a lot to like about Liverpool’s third most expensive signing of all time. For a start, he’s absolutely rapid. Only Harvey Barnes has hit a higher top speed this season than Barcola’s 35.9 km/h.

It has been revealed that that kind of pace should make Barcola one of the most feared wingers in the Premier League, the kind of player that full-backs dread playing against. The kind of player that it used to be said only Kyle Walker could deal with.

And yet, Barcola is all bark but no bite.

He has shown on numerous occasions this season that yes, he may get past you, but he’s not going to do a lot with it.

Barcola has an xG of 2.1 in total for this season, putting him 49th in the league and just 0.1 behind his teammate Florian Wirtz. But unlike the 48 players above him, Barcola has failed to score a goal and even that stat is a little generous.

The thing about Barcola is not only he is bad at shooting, he is particularly bad at getting shots away. The Frenchman has had 56 touches in the opposition box this season, the sixth most of any player in the Premier League, and yet has managed 15 shots in that time. Alexander Isak, who has just one touch more, has got a shot away 31 times.

Industry observers note that this is not a latest trend either. Barcola had the fourth most touches in the box in Ligue 1 last year and got 11 goals, making him the joint eighth top scorer in the division.

In a recent development, that hesitancy to shoot was best displayed in the 4-0 thumping of United. In the 68th minute, when a depleted United back line was caught too high up, Barcola broke clear and got into the box but the ball got caught under his legs, allowing the United defenders to recover and block a shot that in the end had an xG of 0.39. Had he got it away much quicker, that xG would have been a lot higher.

The point isn’t missed on Barcola either. His only contribution from a G/A point of view on Sunday was an assist for Rio Ngumoha after the former PSG man had broken clear.

In a recent development, “I am unsatisfied with my match” he told French broadcaster Canal Plus. “I know that I can do a lot better and I know my abilities. I come out of it with an assist, [but] I could have scored three or four goals.”.

After a 4-0 thumping of your biggest rivals, no one is going to cry too much about the wasted chances but in the tougher matches, either in the latter stages of the Premier League or the Champions League, you cannot afford to have a player be so blunt up front.

Barcola reminds you of another winger who used to play for Liverpool. Change his running style and you would find yourself looking at a copy of Raheem Sterling.

123 goals in the Premier League does not scream someone who is poor in front of goal and while that would be a little harsh, Sterling didn’t half miss some golden opportunities.

He shared that ability to turn a golden chance into one that was stuck under his feet. That wasteful nature is best summed up by Sterling being 19th in the all-time list for Premier League goalscorers but having played more games than 10 players ahead of him.

According to recent reports, the hope for Liverpool is that Iraola can coach Barcola into becoming a better finisher but Sterling worked under Pep Guardiola and was never able to master that ability. Barcola has also come from working under Luis Enrique, hardly a Sunday League manager.

Iraola has noticed Barcola’s wastefulness too, letting slip an answer that was meant as a compliment.

“I think it’s an assist that is a massive merit assist because he was coming from very good movements, arriving against the ‘keeper and not scoring a couple of quite clear situations,” Iraola mentioned.

There is a debate over whether finishing is something you are born with, some arguing that it is a skill in football that can never really be learned, but perhaps Barcola can take solace in the words of France’s greatest ever goalscorer, Thierry Henry.

“I was quick,” Henry told the Blizzard back in 2014. “I had to have 10 chances to convert one into a goal – but at the same time, I kept creating these chances. Then I told myself: ‘You won’t have these chances all the time. You must stick them into the net.’.

What Henry stated next is what Barcola should most listen to for it could be the key to becoming an elite finisher.

“Then, to avoid over-thinking in front of the keeper you work on your finishing, so that it all becomes automatic, so that you don’t think anymore. The hardest thing for an attacking player? When he has time to think.”.

Sources indicate that barcola is one of the quickest players in the league and maybe it is that very pace that is also making him a problem in the box. Barcola has too much time to think and having not scored in the league this season, the voice inside his head reminding him of that fact in crucial moments will only get louder.

Industry observers note that for £123m, you can’t really be described as “not a finisher” and Barcola clearly has to improve in that area. He is playing in the position of Mo Salah, one of the best finishers in Premier League history, and if he can bring even half that effectiveness, it will be a substantial step from where he is today.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

But the early evidence is that things might work out alright in the end for Barca, with Raphinha thriving in his new role as their main striker. He already has an excellent understanding with Yamal, while summer signings Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi have made bright starts.

We’ve put together a Premier League ‘massive six’ mini league for the 2026-27 season, tracking the results between Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham.

The concept of the ‘big six’ feels increasingly outdated. Newcastle United and Aston Villa have challenged the established order in recent years, while Man United, Chelsea and Tottenham have all endured miserable campaigns miles off challenging at the top.

The last time all six clubs actually finished in the top six was back in 2021-22, and it doesn’t appear likely to happen again soon, with the likes of Brentford and Brighton threatening to upset the apple cart this time around.

Industry observers note that but the distinction still holds some weight. These six clubs remain among the Premier League’s biggest spenders in terms of wages and transfer fees, and their financial muscle means they’re rarely far from the conversation. For now, we’ll stick with the traditional definition.

Last season, Manchester United topped our 2025-26 ‘substantial six’ mini league, despite finishing well behind champions Arsenal in the actual table. The Red Devils took 22 points from their 10 matches against their fellow heavyweights, including doubles over Liverpool and Chelsea, with Michael Carrick landing the job on a permanent basis in large part due to some statement victories.

It’s been a different story this season. United have lost all four of their ‘significant six’ encounters, most recently suffering a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. That result proved to be Michael Carrick’s final game in charge, with Mauricio Pochettino appointed as his successor.

Sources indicate that unfortunately for the new boss, his first match could hardly have gone much worse, with United comprehensively beaten on Merseyside. Pochettino has a huge job on his hands, with his side having conceded eight goals in four heavyweight encounters without managing a single victory.

Manchester City, meanwhile, have made a flying start in these fixtures. Enzo Maresca’s men followed up their controversial derby victory by thrashing Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield, an emphatic statement victory that struck a defiant tone following the news of the Premier League finding them guilty of the vast majority of their 115 charges. That stands in stark contrast to their subsequent run of form against teams lower down the table, with dropped points against Aston Villa, Nottingham Forest and Fulham.

Tottenham have also made an encouraging start, taking four points from their first two outings. A late equaliser earned them a draw at Old Trafford before they registered a particularly impressive 2-0 victory away to Chelsea. Things finally seem to be headed in the right direction under Roberto De Zerbi, with a rare victory at Stamford Bridge potentially a turning point.

Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea have endured a mixed start, losing 2-1 at Arsenal and suffering a disappointing 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham before bouncing back with a 2-0 victory over Manchester United.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool have had a mixed start to their big-six fixtures, losing 3-0 to Manchester City and failing to score against Arsenal. But they produced a statement response against Manchester United, running out 4-0 winners at Anfield in a result that gives Andoni Iraola’s project some momentum.

Mikel Arteta’s champions, meanwhile, have maintained their perfect record with a statement 1-0 victory at Anfield, their first league win there since September 2012 and the first under the current boss.

It has been revealed that kai Havertz’s early goal proved decisive, with the Gunners producing something of a Mourinho-esque defensive masterclass to keep Liverpool at arm’s length. Six points from six against Chelsea and Liverpool is an excellent return, and it demonstrates their massive-game mettle after their excellent display in the Community Shield curtain-raiser against Manchester City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal are all sitting in vastly contrasting places when you compare their wage bill rankings to their league positions after the first 11 games of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

Of course, it’s still early in the season. Eleven matches can tell us only so much about how the season will eventually play out, and the table is still taking shape.

Still, there are already some significant, eye-catching differences between wage outlay and performance.

Brighton lead the way. They are second in the Premier League despite having the 15th-highest wage bill, which stands at just £51million. That is a remarkable +13 difference between their league position and wage ranking.

Recent findings suggest that leeds United are next best in that regard. They are sixth while ranking 14th for wages, with a £53million annual bill, giving them a +8 difference. Hull City are similarly overachieving, sitting 11th despite having the 19th-highest wage bill at just £16million. Their +8 difference is another remarkable return for a newly-promoted side.

Brentford are also joint third. They sit 10th while ranking 17th for wages, with an annual bill of just £49million. That’s a +7 difference.

In a recent development, bournemouth are next, sitting fifth while ranking 11th for wages, with an annual wage bill of £63million. That’s a +6 difference, level with Everton, who are seventh despite having the 12th-highest wage bill.

According to recent reports, the traditional powerhouses have produced a mixed bag. Arsenal are top while having the third-highest wage bill in the division, at £154million. That puts them two places ahead of their wage position, while Manchester City sit third in the league and second in the wage rankings.

It has been revealed that chelsea are eighth with the seventh-highest wage bill, £97million, while top spenders Liverpool are fourth. The Reds have the highest wage bill in the Premier League at £177million but sit three places below that ranking.

It has been revealed that the other ‘Massive Six’ underachievers are not hard to spot. Manchester United are 19th with the fourth-highest wage bill of £152million, while Tottenham are ninth despite having the fifth-highest at £138million.

It has been revealed that villa are also slightly off the pace. They are 12th despite having the sixth-highest wage bill, with £98million going on salaries. That puts them six places below their wage ranking.

Malen d’Or? Forgotten Villa player on Mbappe’s tail in European Golden Boot race

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (733 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it’s just getting a bit silly now.
  • Yep, that’s nearly as many as Inter’s Marcus Thuram and Como’s Anastasios Douvikas – the pair on 13 in the same timeframe – put together.
  • In fact, no player in Europe’s top five leagues can match him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it’s just getting a bit silly now. Since Aston Villa sold Donyell Malen to Roma in January, the most any other player in Serie A has scored is 13 goals. Malen has scored 25.

Yep, that’s nearly as many as Inter’s Marcus Thuram and Como’s Anastasios Douvikas – the pair on 13 in the same timeframe – put together.

In fact, no player in Europe’s top five leagues can match him. The leader in that time in the Premier League is Erling Haaland with 16; it’s Raphinha in La Liga with 21; Harry Kane in the Bundesliga with 20; and Esteban Lepaul in Ligue 1 with 19.

It’s the sheer consistency that makes Malen’s impact at Roma so impressive. His drive and determination have helped him showcase what he wanted to all along: he’s an elite goalscorer.

Recent findings suggest that he was in a mean mood on Saturday, scoring four past Parma. His first saw him expertly guide the ball beyond his marker after a cross before slotting home, with the rest all showing his clinical nature in the box.

It has been revealed that this is just what Malen does for Roma. He’s found a system where he’s the central figure, playing in his preferred position that he never got a chance to consistently with Villa. He’s backed himself ever since the move and he’s been good for his word.

His efforts against Parma gave him his third hat-trick for Roma, but he went one better and became their first player to score four goals in a Serie A game for almost 25 years.

Donyell Malen hit FOUR past Parma 😮‍💨#ParmaRoma #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/gulnLRKO2J.

— Lega Serie A (@SerieA_EN) November 22, 2026.

Industry observers note that if you weren’t already, it’s time to start taking him seriously in any debates about the best strikers in Europe. Sure, he doesn’t quite have the same potency for the Netherlands, so you could argue he’s a system player, but when he scores as often as he does in that system, it’s got to count for something.

Sources indicate that sure enough, Malen is becoming one to watch in the race for the European Golden Shoe. Only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe have scored more than him in Europe’s top five leagues so far, and he’s only one goal behind the latter.

Recent findings suggest that mbappe won the European Golden Shoe two years ago, in between Harry Kane’s two triumphs. It would take a herculean effort for Kane to retain the accolade due to his current injury, so someone like Malen’s eyes should be lighting up.

According to recent reports, he really is hot on the heels of Mbappe right now. You’d imagine the Frenchman will stay the course, while current leader Raphinha has been sensational so far since being converted into a striker himself at Barcelona, but will it last?

Some might ask similar questions about Malen, but he’s been doing this for nearly a year now. There might have been doubts over his ability to carry this form from last season into this one, and he’s made a mockery of them.

Carry on at this rate, and the Serie A golden boot that he came close to capturing last season – despite having half as much time to aim for it as his rivals – could be his. Beyond that, the European Golden Shoe, or even a Ballon d’Or nomination (for the 30-man shortlist, at least) might not be out of reach.

In a recent development, this Roma side have produced the best start to a season in the modern era in terms of goals scored at this stage. Of course, Malen has been front and centre of those efforts.

His latest Instagram post featured music in the background – a song named after him where the singer muses: “Maybe now I only love Bobby Malen.” (Oh, yeah, they call him Bobby over there – it’s a long story).

Just a classic case of a footballer finding a club he fits in at like a glove, and loving life. File that under things you love to see. Unless, perhaps, you’re a Villa fan. Or maybe even a Golden Shoe-hunting Mbappe….

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next big thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

Recent findings suggest that the latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

Of course, injuries, personal challenges and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

It has been revealed that in 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

The hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

But things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

According to recent reports, after making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

According to recent reports, from that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

In a recent development, since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Recent findings suggest that morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is currently plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

The first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

It has been revealed that however, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

It has been revealed that but his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

The Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

In a recent development, the Brazilian is at the moment imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

The hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

But the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

The Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never revealed his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

It has been revealed that he enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the significant transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

However, Sanches struggled to find his feet in Germany and was soon sent out on loan to Swansea, where he is perhaps best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a significant-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

Industry observers note that the Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

In a recent development, the Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

After six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

It has been revealed that it seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

It has been revealed that after a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

It has been revealed that kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is noted and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.
  • Sources indicate that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.

Sources indicate that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the company sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said his organization would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have declared plans to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has announced that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler announced on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the company statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, announced last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.
